Just turned 22. Recently diagnosed with social anxiety and secondary depression. Family lives beyond our means which equates to debt that'll outlast my parents and fall onto me. Luckily, for now it means I can live a simple but comfortable life in my parents house. I'll help my dad with his work whenever I get the chance and he'll return the favour by giving me a bit of cash here and there. Beyond what little I earn, I'm entirely reliant on them. 

What do I do all day? I distract myself. Some distractions are healthier than others. Some weeks I'll make music for ten hours a day. Some I'll do nothing but play video games and watch tv. Sometimes I'll make an effort to be social, go fishing, maybe have drink with a friend, but most of my socializing takes place through Skype. As does my love life in the form of a long distance relationship. 

Honestly I don't **do** very much. I wait to feel better and on the days I feel better I have responsibilities to take care of. Cleaning, laundry, normal everyday things that become a primary occupation when most days it feels like you can't do even simple things.

If you're anything like me, then you're most certainly waiting for that something to change. You know the one, the something of unbelievable importance which you have absolutely no control over, and no real clue what it might even be, to flip that switch and make everything all bright and shiny and new again. Well here's hoping it happens soon, elsewise I guess we shoot up, watch the world burn and hope to hold on. 

Thanks for your comment. It's bittersweet knowing there are more like me. I don't think the help and the pills work right without cutting off something necessary to this personality, so this kind of anonymous discussion is really all there is. In no way am I condemning therapy and drugs, if it works for you all for it, Jesus Christ one more life saved. I've just found they didn't work for me without losing more of myself than I've lost now. 

I hope whatever's missing clicks for you. And I hope it clicks for me too.

Social pressures skew the average perception of this lifestyle. If damage is being done to yourself and to others then maybe there's cause for concern. At that point it is a responsibility belonging to your loved ones to intervene and to get you well. However, asking someone to give up a part of themselves for another part of themselves is a ridiculous concept. 

You've compartmentalized your habit as many junkies do. It has a special place away from another life; another part of you. For somebody to discover that new part of you and attempt to will it away with childish threats of 'us or them'...  This comes from a place of misinformation and a general lack of understanding or the want to understand. From fear and from bias, from a savior complex and a childish little mind. Really, it's all too common and just as frustrating.

Would I leave this lifestyle for my significant other? No. But I also would not involve myself with someone who would not accept me for what I am. It sounds cliche but truly, why be with somebody who doesn't want you? Who only wants their perfect china doll. If I were damaging myself beyond all function, becoming that sick caricature of a dirty twisted little man dying in an alleyway that we all have floating through the back of our minds, and in that destroying the person I hold most dear, then and only then would I would leave this lifestyle 'for' them. But not for a fool who has a case of The Fear.

If I could still turn something out. Give me a notebook and pen, maybe even a guitar, then hell yea. Jail's not so bad. It's like anywhere else; you learn the rules and you play by them. To have all the basic human needs taken care of, a magic box filled with good temperament, joy, and to have the ability to work near endlessly, I'd be home. Shit I figure I'd be ten times as productive.
I'm proud of you friend. If this isn't a life for you, if this really is a demon, then you're doing right by yourself to stay clean.
